chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abi al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the time of Zuhr and 'Asr, so he said: The time of Zuhr is when the sun declines until the shadow goes to one qamah, and the time of 'Asr is from one and a half qamahs until two qamahs.

key_terms.الشَّمْسُ: the sun, whose movement marks prayer times
key_terms.الظِّلُّ: the shadow used as an indicator for the prayer time
key_terms.قَامَةً: a measured unit based on height used here to determine shadow length
key_terms.قَامَتَيْنِ: two qamahs, indicating the upper limit mentioned for the prayer time
key_terms.وَقْتِ: the designated time period for performing an act of worship

ai.seo_question: What are the times of Zuhr and 'Asr prayer according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the time limits for salat al-Zuhr and salat al-'Asr by describing them in relation to the sun's decline and the length of the shadow. It serves as a jurisprudential basis for determining the valid times of these two daily prayers.
